title: The LORD's Anointed King on Zion
summary: The nations and their rulers conspire against the LORD and his Anointed One, resolving to throw off his rule. God in heaven laughs at them and announces that he has installed his King on Zion. The king then reports the LORD's decree, “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father,” with the nations promised as his inheritance. The psalm ends by urging the kings of the earth to serve the LORD with fear and to kiss the Son, and it closes with a blessing on all who take refuge in him.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Royal psalms are about the king of Israel: his crowning, his wedding, his battles, God's promise to his family (Psalms 2, 18, 20, 21, 45, 72, 89, 101, 110, 132, 144).

line: The nations plot against the LORD and his anointed king, God answers from heaven by installing his King on Zion, and the psalm ends with a blessing on all who take refuge in him.
guide: Ask where the old wish to throw off God's rule lives quietly in you. When the world seems to rage against what is good, pray it as the first Christians did, for courage rather than revenge. End where the psalm ends, with its open door to everyone who runs to God's king for refuge.

verses.t: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together, against the LORD and against His Anointed One:
“Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords.”
The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord taunts them.
Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury:
“I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain.”
I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.
Ask Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance, the ends of the earth Your possession.
You will break them with an iron scepter; You will shatter them like pottery.”
Therefore be wise, O kings; be admonished, O judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in your rebellion, when His wrath ignites in an instant. Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.
